title: Saturated submodules over valuation-ring restricted series are finite
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, let $V=\{a\in K:|a|\le1\}$ be its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], and fix $\pi\in V$ with $0<|\pi|<1$. For an integer $r\ge0$ let $S=V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$, the ring of formal series with coefficients tending to zero [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. If $P\subseteq M$ is an $S$-submodule saturated for powers of $\pi$, meaning that for every $x\in M$ and $k\ge0$, $\pi^k x\in P$ implies $x\in P$, then $P$ is finitely generated as an $S$-module. No finite-presentation or torsion-freeness hypothesis is imposed on $M$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Lemma 7(i), printed pp. 131–132 (PDF pages 132–133), case (V); Theorem 4 on printed p. 130 supplies its finiteness input. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $Q=M/P$ and let $q:M\twoheadrightarrow Q$ be the quotient map. The images of any finite generating family of $M$ generate $Q$ by taking representatives and applying $q$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For $0\ne a\in V$ choose $k\ge0$ with $|\pi|^k\le|a|$; then $b=\pi^k/a\in V$ and $ba=\pi^k$. If $a\bar x=0$ in $Q$, a representative $x\in M$ satisfies $ax\in P$, hence $\pi^kx=bax\in P$. Saturation gives $x\in P$, so $\bar x=0$. Thus $Q$ is torsion-free over $V$. This uses no cancellation on $M$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Lemma 7(i), printed pp. 131–132 (PDF pages 132–133), case (V); online primary PDF.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] to the valuation ring $V$ and the torsion-free $V$-module $Q$ of Step 1. It gives flatness of $Q$ over $V$, with no finite-generation requirement over $V$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Lemma 7(i), printed pp. 131–132 (PDF pages 132–133), case (V); online primary PDF.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-restricted-flat-module-finite-presentation] to the given complete valued field $K$, its ring $V$, the same number $r$ of variables and $Q$. Step 1 supplies finite generation over $S$, and Step 2 supplies flatness over $V$ through constants. It follows that $Q$ is finitely presented over $S$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Lemma 7(i), printed pp. 131–132 (PDF pages 132–133), case (V); online primary PDF.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel] with ring $S$, finitely generated source $M$, finitely presented target $Q$ from Step 3, and surjection $q$. Its kernel is finitely generated. Since $q(x)=0$ holds exactly when $x\in P$, this kernel is $P$, proving the claim.

source.place: Section 2.3, Lemma 7(i), printed pp. 131–132 (PDF pages 132–133), case (V); online primary PDF.

proof_origin.place: Bosch 2.3/7(i), case (V), read in the online primary PDF; explicit scalar-divisibility argument and direct application of the existing general kernel lemma. Local archival copy WANTED.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Completeness of restricted-series quotients over a rank-one valuation ring. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. Specifically, the induced-submodule topology input of Bosch 2.3/7(ii), used in the proof of 2.3/8 supporting 2.3/9. The saturated-submodule finiteness input in Bosch 2.3/7(i), used to prove 2.3/7(ii).

split_report.summary: Verified Bosch 2.3/7(i) and Theorem 4 online. Proved quotient torsion-freeness explicitly using powers of pi cofinal with all nonzero scalar divisors. Reused valuation torsion-free flatness and generic finite-presentation kernel finiteness leaves; created one statement-only analytic finite-presentation input, with searches and no finite type/Noetherian substitution. Ambient M is only finitely generated.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NX-3158ca5fb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, every cited statement and the report. Step 1 is elementary and correct. M/P is finite over S. For a≠0 in V pick k with |pi|^k<=|a|, so pi^k/a lies in V, and saturation then gives V-torsion-freeness without any cancellation in M. Step 2 applies lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat; its inline valuation-ring definition is met by V, and it needs no finiteness. Step 3 applies the new node lem-trf-restricted-flat-module-finite-presentation, with Q finite over S and flat over V through constants. Step 4 applies lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel to the quotient map M->M/P; its kernel is P. The new node is the rank-one case (V) of Bosch 2.3/4 (Raynaud-Gruson): K complete with a nontrivial real absolute value, so V is pi-adically complete and V<T> is the pi-adic restricted-series ring. Its hypotheses match one for one, nothing is weakened, it has statement only, and every notion cites its definition node. I tested it on r=0 (finite torsion-free over a valuation ring is free), Q=0, and S/(pi), which is not flat and so is excluded. I tested the item on M=S/(pi), where P is forced to be M, and on m of a non-discrete V, which is not saturated. My rg -L duplicate search (Raynaud/Gruson, restricted plus finitely presented, saturated, topologically finite type) found no duplicate. The new node is not a restatement of the item and creates no cycle. No copy of Bosch is under literature/, so I could not read the document; the report has a WANTED line and proof_origin.by=agent, as the brief requires. The report names citations.json and searches.jsonl, which are not in the commit; these are tool files, not a DAG fault. No fixes and no tool_uses.
